subsystems.name: Gas supply
subsystems.role: provides the raw materials the microbes eat: carbon dioxide and hydrogen, plus oxygen.
parts: CO2 stream from industrial flue gas or direct air capture
oxygen and gas blending and safety interlocks

subsystems.name: Electrolyser
subsystems.role: splits water into hydrogen and oxygen using renewable electricity; it is the main energy input.

subsystems.name: Bioreactor
subsystems.role: a stirred or loop fermenter where bacteria contact dissolved gases in water.

subsystems.name: Culture
subsystems.role: the living catalyst — hydrogen-oxidising bacteria that build cell mass from CO2.

subsystems.name: Harvest and dry
subsystems.role: separates the grown biomass from water and turns it into a stable powder.

subsystems.name: Process control and safety
subsystems.role: keeps a hydrogen–oxygen–CO2 gas mix inside safe limits while holding growth conditions steady.

buildSteps.title: Select and bank the strain
buildSteps.detail: A hydrogen-oxidising bacterium is chosen for food safety, fast growth and high protein content, then kept as frozen seed cultures.

buildSteps.title: Make hydrogen and capture CO2
buildSteps.detail: An electrolyser runs on low-carbon electricity to split water; the CO2 comes from a captured industrial stream or from the air, then is cleaned of impurities that would poison the culture.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the growth medium
buildSteps.detail: Water is mixed with ammonia, phosphate and trace metals; the broth is sterilised so unwanted microbes do not outgrow the culture.

buildSteps.title: Run the gas fermentation
buildSteps.detail: Hydrogen and CO2 are bubbled into the bioreactor at around 30 °C and controlled pH. Because hydrogen dissolves poorly in water, designs use fine bubbles, high pressure or loop reactors to keep enough gas in solution, and continuously draw off the extra water the electrolyser and metabolism produce.

buildSteps.title: Keep the gas mixture safe
buildSteps.detail: Hydrogen, oxygen and CO2 are metered so the headspace stays outside flammable limits, with analysers and trips that shut the feed if composition drifts.

buildSteps.title: Harvest the biomass
buildSteps.detail: Broth is drawn off continuously and the cells are separated by centrifuge or membrane filtration.

buildSteps.title: Inactivate and dry
buildSteps.detail: The paste is heat-treated to kill the cells and dried into a powder that is mostly protein, along with fibre, fat and minerals.

buildSteps.title: Formulate and get approval
buildSteps.detail: The powder is blended into foods or feed, which requires a novel-food safety assessment in each market before sale.

prerequisites.why: the electrolyser is the dominant cost and energy input; the process makes sense only where power is cheap and clean.
it supplies the hydrogen that carries energy into the microbes.
industrial CO2 streams exist today, but direct air capture is early and expensive.
gas-to-protein fermentation is proven at industrial scale on methane, but hydrogen–CO2 systems are still at demonstration and first-plant scale.
approvals exist in a few jurisdictions only, so market access is fragmented.

pathway.milestone: first small commercial plants producing tonnes per year, with a handful of novel-food approvals
pathway.unlocks: real products in niche foods and proof the process runs reliably.

pathway.milestone: plants in the tens of thousands of tonnes per year, sited next to cheap solar, wind or hydro
pathway.unlocks: costs approaching conventional protein for some ingredients.

pathway.milestone: scale-up in animal feed, where approvals are simpler and volumes are large
pathway.unlocks: a route to volume that does not depend on consumer acceptance.

pathway.milestone: deployment where farming is impossible — deserts, islands, spacecraft life support
pathway.unlocks: protein production decoupled from land, weather and season.
